purpose: Console-side file saving through already-installed native services. The static website does not bypass browser filesystem restrictions.

ps4.storageDetection: Not supported by this receiver: there is no directory-listing or mount-enumeration endpoint. The user must inspect the real existing path in ezRemote and confirm it before queuing.
ps4.destinationCheck: HEAD /<full-destination-file> and HEAD /<full-destination-file>.tmp detect collisions. A 404 does not establish that the destination parent exists or is writable.

ps5.destinationCheck: websrv v0.34 on port8080: GET /fs/<existing-folder>/?fmt=json, array of name/mode/size entries
ps5.storageDetection: GET http://<console>:8080/fs/mnt/?fmt=json. Offer only usbN/extN entries with mode m: websrv reports directories on a device different from the parent as m; d alone may be an empty mount point. Numbers are mount identifiers, not physical USB slot numbers. Directory listings do not prove write access or available space.
ps5.fileBrowser: GET http://<console>:8080/fs/<validated-existing-folder>/ opens websrv's real HTML filesystem listing in a new tab. This is a read-only navigation action; saving remains an explicit separate click.

queue.acknowledgment: Empty HTTP200 acknowledges submission only. Explicit result.success:false is rejected.
queue.status: GET same-origin /get_download_state. Re-read immediately before each download submission; a matching destination record prevents a duplicate POST. Network/unreadable-response submission failures remain uncertain and locked while later status reads can recover the actual record.
limitations: Destination parents must already exist; the background download code does not create them.
Receiver-reported completion is not hash verification or proof of console compatibility.
Public HTTPS pages navigate to the installed local companion; they do not perform unsupported cross-origin POSTs to console services.
Desktop localhost preview addresses are not reachable from a different console. Catalogue files must be published, or served through a console-reachable LAN host for testing.

preparation.downloadFolder: /data/whatwhatboy or <verified mounted storage folder>/whatwhatboy. It is created only after an explicit action on the local client-origin preparation page; the background receiver cannot create it.
preparation.ps4ClientOrigin: http://<console>:8080; pinned ezRemote Client 2.08 mounts filesystem / at URL /. The installed companion is available at /data/whatsite-ps4.html?prepare=1&folder=<encoded-folder>.
preparation.ps5ClientOrigin: http://<console>:9090; pinned ezRemote Client 2.18 mounts filesystem / at URL /. The installed companion is available at /data/homebrew/ezremote-client/assets/whatsite-ps5.html?prepare=1&folder=<encoded-folder>.
preparation.originBoundary: Client APIs are separate from background receiver 6701 and PS5 websrv 8080. Preparation executes same-origin on the client port, then offers explicit navigation back to the matching receiver URL carrying the verified folder. Public pages cannot call these write APIs. Configured non-default client ports use the native file-manager fallback.
preparation.list: POST same-origin /__local__/list with JSON {path,onlyFolders:false}; response {result:[{name,type:'dir'|'file',size,rights,date}]}. A nonexistent directory can return an empty listing because the upstream handler ignores its FS::ListDir error, so root/ancestor existence is established from the parent's directory entry.
preparation.mkdir: POST same-origin /__local__/createFolder with JSON {newPath}. The upstream MkDirs loops mkdir and ignores errors; success:true alone is insufficient. Check each existing parent, skip existing directories, refuse colliding files, create only missing child directories, and verify the new directory through its parent listing. Never create /data or /mnt/usbN placeholders. Never call remove, rename, edit or install APIs.
preparation.storage: PS5 rechecks websrv mounted-device evidence before external creation/extraction. PS4 requires explicit confirmation of the actual device in ezRemote; directory names do not establish mount or port identity. Existing file/directory permissions and available space remain native-service checks.
preparation.extract: POST same-origin /__local__/extract with JSON {item:<saved-full-archive-path>,destination:<output-parent>,folderName:<new-child-name>}. Supports ZIP/RAR/7z through libarchive. Never reuse an existing output child. Preserve the original archive. The API is synchronous and has no extraction-percentage endpoint; show an indeterminate operation state, then verify its reported result and a nonempty output listing. Do not retry automatically on lost connections or failed/partial output.
preparation.archiveSafety: Pinned extractors reject basic absolute/traversal paths but restore symlinks and can overwrite output. Automatic extraction therefore requires item.archiveSafety from docs/console-archive-safety.json: reviewed/noLinks/relativePaths/noDevices/noAlternateStreams/noEncryptedEntries all true; sha256 and bytes match the archive; entryCount1..5000 and expandedBytes0..128MiB. The source archive entry audit rejects symlinks, hardlinks, device/special files, absolute paths, traversal, alternate streams and encrypted entries. Only reviewed archives <=32 MiB are read as same-origin ArrayBuffer and SHA-256 checked against their reviewed bytes before any output directories are created or extraction requested. Unreviewed/larger/changed archives keep native file-manager access; no containment guarantee is invented for them.
preparation.verification: Metadata-only request/response fixtures, native SHA-256 comparison vectors, no physical-console mutations. Directory and extraction operations have not been hardware tested. Native client behavior has no atomic no-overwrite flag, so output names are unique and checked before each explicit request.

hostFindings.goldhen: GET http://127.0.0.1:9090/status then POST rawBIN to9090 runs a payload; it does not save it to disk. Instant loading is HTTP-only.

verification: Unit contracts and a loopback metadata-only receiver fixture. No downloaded payloads were executed. Physical PS4/PS5 transfers have not been tested.
